disease_label_per_paper: ESBL-producing Escherichia coli bacteremia with septic shock and Eustachian valve infective endocarditis in an ESRD hemodialysis patient
presentation_summary: 47-year-old woman with hypertension, type 2 diabetes, hyperlipidemia, seizures, and ESRD on hemodialysis presented from dialysis with a bleeding right upper arm arterio-venous graft.
On arrival she had altered mental status, fever 103.0 F, hypotension 74/45 mmHg, sinus tachycardia in the 120s, and tachypnea 23/min; she required norepinephrine for septic shock.
She received vancomycin and cefepime initially and ICU monitoring with hemodialysis; at most she required 4 L oxygen by nasal cannula.
Left upper extremity ultrasound of the arterio-venous graft showed no abscess; later CT chest/abdomen/pelvis found no occult source.
Blood cultures were positive for ESBL-producing E. coli in two bottles, sensitive to meropenem; TEE later confirmed Eustachian valve vegetation.

quality_warnings: This case is a post-microbiology ESBL bacteremia test: blood culture gram-negative bacteremia, ESBL phenotype, ceftriaxone non-susceptibility, and carbapenem susceptibility are rankable because they define the resistance leaf.
Daily culture clearance, TEE vegetation, treatment response, and outcome remain non-ranking confirmatory evidence.
